name: The office

masthead.lede: You know your work better than anyone. This worksheet helps you lay out what’s slow, repetitive, or error-prone, so that {consultantFirst} can build something that actually helps instead of guessing. There are no wrong answers, and you don’t need to know anything about software.
howto: Answer in your own words. Specific beats polished. “Last Tuesday” beats “usually.”
Describe problems, not solutions. Figuring out the fix is the builder’s job. You only have to describe what actually happens.
Nothing is graded. A half-answer is more useful than a blank. Questions marked optional can be skipped if you’re short on time.
Your answers save in this browser as you type. Close the tab, come back later, pick up where you left off. (They stay on this device only.)
rules: One occasion, not a pattern. Wherever you can, tell me about a specific time it happened, with a day and a number.
In Parts 2–4, don’t use the words app, software, system, automate, dashboard, or AI. If you catch yourself writing “we need something that…”, stop and write down what happened instead.
Real beats tidy. The messy workaround you’re slightly embarrassed by is usually the most valuable thing on this page.
masthead.after: When you’re done, {consultantFirst} reads it within two business days and sends you one page: what he heard, and the two or three things worth building first.

finishText: Nothing has been sent yet — your answers are only in this browser. The button below turns them into a plain text summary you can copy into an email to {consultantFirst} ({consultantEmail}), download as a file, or print. Empty questions are marked so you can see what you skipped.
